numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Dividing a Timedelta by a float ndarray whose quotient leaves the int64 range silently saturates to the int64 maximum instead of raising. Example: Timedelta(4, 'ns') / np.array([1e-300]) returns array([9223372036854775807], dtype='timedelta64[ns]').
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta with the message 'Overflow in timedelta division', matching the existing TimedeltaIndex behaviour. Zero and nan divisors are exempt and still return NaT.
trigger_conditions: Timedelta divided by a float ndarray (dtype kind 'f') using / or //
Quotient magnitude |td._value / divisor| is at or above 2**63 for some element
Divisor is not zero and not nan (those return NaT)
Integer ndarray divisors are not affected and need no check
Timedelta.__floordiv__ path with a float ndarray other

oracle_clues: Expected behaviour mirrors TimedeltaIndex / np.array([1e-300]), which raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta: Overflow in timedelta division

numerical_characteristics.dtype: float64 (f8) and float32 (f4) divisor arrays; check computed in float64 regardless of divisor precision
numerical_characteristics.precision: A float32 quotient would overflow to inf before measurement, so the check is performed in float64; the passages do not state a numeric precision tolerance
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Quotient leaving the int64 range, e.g. Timedelta(4, "ns") / np.array([1e-300]) saturating to 9223372036854775807 ns; test uses Timedelta(4, unit) / np.array([1e-30]); Timedelta.min boundary (-2**63, 2**63) referenced
category_specific_evidence: Formula violated: Timedelta divided by a float array must report out-of-range quotients rather than saturating to the int64 limit; quotient magnitude |td._value / other| must lie within int64 range (-2**63, 2**63)
Reproduction: Timedelta(4, "ns") / np.array([1e-300]) returns array([9223372036854775807], dtype='timedelta64[ns]') (saturated) instead of raising
Expected after fix: pd.TimedeltaIndex([Timedelta(4, "ns")]) / np.array([1e-300]) raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta with message 'Overflow in timedelta division'; Timedelta / and // now raise the same
Test test_td_div_float_ndarray_overflow parametrized over units s, ms, us, ns and dtypes f8, f4 with other=np.array([1e-30]) expects OutOfBoundsTimedelta for td / other and td // other

Zero and nan divisors are exempt and must yield NaT: np.array([0]), np.array([0.0]), np.array([np.nan]) return array of np.timedelta64('NaT','ns'); float zero divisor emits numpy divide warning suppressed via np.errstate in TimedeltaIndex path
In-bounds case: Timedelta(12, "ns") / np.array([[2.0],[3.0]]) gives [[6],[4]] dtype m8[ns]; // same; empty f8 array returns empty m8[ns]
Integer divisors need no check since quotient exceeds dividend only when divisor is between -1 and 1
Fix applied in pandas/_libs/tslibs/timedeltas.pyx via _check_div_float_array called from __truediv__ and __floordiv__ when other.dtype.kind == 'f'
reproduction_risks: A zero float divisor emits numpy zero-division RuntimeWarning unless wrapped in np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore')
Test must not treat zero/nan divisors as overflow; they must return NaT
Quotients near the int64 boundary: float64 quotient inside (-2**63, 2**63) is at least one ulp from boundary, so floor in __floordiv__ should not push it out of bounds
Tz-aware DatetimeArray._add_offset fast path remains open (not covered by this fix) and is out of scope
Requires pandas build with the timedeltas.pyx change; passages do not give version numbers
